sentences.text:
The petitioner being RC owner of Car No.KA-55-M- 9325 filed petition under Sec.166 of I.M.V. Act claiming damages worth of Rs.8,00,000/- from the respondents No.1 and 2 who are owner and insurer of a Container Lorry No.KA-01-AJ-1805 asserting that on 15.10.2021 at about 05.00 a.m.,
when driving the Car No.KA-55-M-9325 on Dommasandra - Chandapura road, Railway Bridge, near Heelalige Tank, Anekal Taluk, due to rain water car struck in the road, driver of the Container Lorry No.KA-01-AJ- 1805 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the hind part of the car thereby caused accident caused damage to the car.
Petitioner get repaired the car by spending Rs.4,21,781/-.

2. Regarding the accident Suryanagara Police registered Crime No.282/2021 against the driver of the lorry for having committed the offence punishable under Sec. 279 of PC.
3.

In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of the accident,
nature of the damage suffered by car and quantum of the damages suffered by the petitioner.
4. Inspite of service notice, respondent No.1 owner of the Container Lorry No.KA-01-AJ-1805 remained absent.

5. On the basis of the pleadings on 09.08.2023 this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 15.10.2021 at about 05.00 a.m., on Dommasandra - Chandapura Road, Railway Bridge, near Heelalige Tank, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru district, he met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing registration No. KA-01-AJ-1805 as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
6. On 18.05.2023, 17.10.2023 petitioner deposed as PW.1 and produced 12 documents at Exhibits P.1 to P.12.
On 23.08.2024, petitioner produced copy of the policy pertaining to car at Ex.P13.
On 09.02.2024, 19.02.2024 respondent No.2 produced evidence of Officer as RW.1.

sentences.text: I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

8. On the basis of the materials placed on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.50,000/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a. as damages from respondents, Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 9. Issue No.1:-

In the evidence affidavit, petitioner/ PW.1 stated that on 15.10.2021 at about 05.00 a.m., when driving the Maruti Car No.KA-55-M-9325 from Dommasandra towards Chandapura,
near Railway Bridge, Heelalige Tank, Anekal Taluk due to rain water, car struck in the road, driver of Container Lorry No.KA-01-AJ-1805 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the rear part of the car thereby caused accident and caused damage to the car.
10.
In the written statement, respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding the reason and mode of accident.

11. In the cross-examination, petitioner/PW.1 stated that on the date of accident himself and his helper Shiva are travelling by sitting in the car which was stopped at the entrance of the underpass railway bridge due to heavy rain, stopped the car after observing heavy water in underpass railway bridge.
Petitioner stated that earlier to stopping of car, the car was running at a speed of 60 kmph and behind the car several vehicles are running.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that he suddenly stopped the car therefore lorry which was running behind the car came in contact with the car.
In the cross-examination PW.1 admitted that in the photo marked at Ex.R1 and R2 railway bridge are visible and admitted that underpass bridge is narrow and only one vehicle can pass in that road.

12. In the evidence RW.1 Manager of the Insurance Company an hear say witness of the incident,
narrated the same facts as narrated in the written statement.

13. Ex.P1 & P3 are the copy of the complaint and FIR pertaining to Crime No.282/2021 registered by Suryanagara Police against the driver of the lorry No. KA- 01-AJ-1805 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279 of IPC, regarding the collision between rear part of the Maruti Car No.KA-55-M-9325 and front part of the Container Lorry No.KA-01-AJ-1805 resulting in the damage to the car on the basis of the complaint filed by petitioner.
14. Ex.P2 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Suryanagara Police in crime No.282/2021 against driver of lorry No. KA-01-AJ-1805 for having committed offence punishable under Sec. 279 of IPC.
Ex.P4 is the copy of the spot mahazar.
Ex . P8
is the copy of the Motor Vehicle Accident Report dated 16.10.2021.
In the photo marked at Ex.P10 the place of incident car and lorry are visible.
15. In the file, there are no evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by petitioner regarding the reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 15.10.2021 at about Ashok Alias Ashok S.R vs M.M.K. Logistics on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149312779/
3 05.00 a.m., when petitioner was driving Maruti Car No.KA-55-M-9325 from Dommasandra towards Chandapura near Railway Bridge, Heelalige Tank, Anekal Taluk due to rain water car struck in the road Pradeep Kumar S/o Krishnappa negligently drove the lorry No. KA-01-AJ-1805 dashed the same to the rear part of the Maruti Car No.KA-55-M-9325 thereby caused accident and caused damage to the car.

sentences.text: Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:

In the evidence affidavit, petitioner/ PW.1 stated that in the accident car No.
KA-55-M-9325 was completely damaged, then get repaired the car at Suraksha Car Care Ltd., by spending Rs.4,21,781/-.
17.
In the written statement, the respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegations regarding the nature of the damage suffered by the car and quantum of the damages suffered by the petitioner.
18. In the cross-examination petitioner/P.W.1 stated that in the accident left and front part of the car are damaged and submitted non-claiming of the damages from the insurer of his car.
Petitioner stated that the estimation marked at Ex.P9 has been issued stating that the money required for repair and the damage.
19. In the evidence affidavit, RW.1 stating nothing regarding the quantum of the damages suffered by the petitioner.

20. Motor Vehicle Accident Report marked at Ex.P8 shows that on 16.08.2021 during inspection Motor Vehicle Inspector noticed following damage in car No. KA-55-M- 9325 i) Front bumper damaged,
ii) Left side head light damages,
iii) Front left side fender damaged,
iv) Left side doors damages,
v) Rear dickey damaged,
vi) Left side tail lamp and indicator damaged,
vii) Rear bumper damaged,
viii) Left side quarter damaged,
ix) Front wind screen glass broken,
x) Rear wind scree glass broken.

sentences.text: Ex.P9 is the estimate given by Suraksha Car Care Pvt., Ltd., for Rs.4,21,781/- to repair the car.
Ex . P10 photos of the car and lorry which are involved in the accident.
Ex.P11 is the RC of the car which shows that during December 2016 car No. KA-55-M-9325 has been manufactured and purchased by the petitioner.
Ex.P13 is the copy of the policy pertaining to car No. KA-55-M-9325 for the period 31.12.2020 to 30.12.2021 in which IDV is noted at Rs.1,76,644/-.

The above referred material shows that after more than 4 years from the date of purchase the car met with an accident resulting in the damage.
21.

Considering date of manufacture of the car, particulars of the damage noticed by the Motor Vehicle Inspector on 16.10.2021 during inspection noted in the Motor Vehicle Accident Report IDV of the car noted at Rs.1,76,644/- in the policy dated 30.12.2020 (depreciation) I have estimated damages at Rs.50,000/-.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner being RC owner of the car No. KA-55-M-9325 is entitled to receive Rs.50,000/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a.
as damages.
22. In the evidence affidavit, RW.1 Officer of the insurance company admitted subsistence of the policy with respect to lorry No. KA-01-AJ-1805 as on the date of accident.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondent No.1 and 2 being owner and insurer of the lorry No. KA-01-AJ-1805 are liable to pay damages to the petitioner and award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay damages to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.
The respondent No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioner towards compensation.

The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the lorry No.
KA-01-AJ-1805 shall deposit the damages with interest within three months from today.
After deposit of the damages, entire damages and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by him, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 07 th day of October, 2024)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
